_comment: Fundraising proposal for Pinemount Developments Ltd. (Moshin Sheri). From the Sep 25 2026 strategy call with Matt. Two LinkedIn profiles (Moshin + newly onboarded IR / dealing rep), two purpose-built rental raises (Peterborough, Scarborough), $3,000 USD/month, 6-month term with 3-month opt-out. Site-to-amount mapping deliberately not stated.

cards.label: THE ASK
cards.text: About $5.5M in new equity across two purpose-built rental projects in Peterborough and Scarborough, each over $100M in project cost: roughly $3.5M within 6–8 months and $2M in about four, the top-ups needed to close CMHC-backed construction financing. Beyond these two, a wider bench of investors for the two to three raises Pinemount runs every year.

cards.label: THE PLAN
cards.text: Two LinkedIn profiles, Moshin’s and your new IR rep’s, run end to end by ThinkFISH in your voice. Targeting accredited and high-net-worth investors, family offices and business owners with a history in private real estate, plus pre-booked meetings at the events your IR rep attends. Every meeting pre-qualified and approved by you; your team closes.

cards.label: THE INVESTMENT
cards.text: $3,000 USD per month, flat, for both profiles. Six-month term with a three-month opt-out. Covers both raises. No setup fee, no success fee, no commission, no carve-out of the equity you’ve already raised, no transaction involvement.

band.label: WHAT TO EXPECT
band.text: Outreach live within two weeks of kickoff and the full flow from about day 30: 2–4 qualified meetings per week across both profiles, weekly reporting and a data-driven checkpoint in December. One honest note for ownership: raises historically take 6–12 months from first outreach to capital in the bank. Your track record helps, but a new investor still needs time to diligence a new sponsor, so new relationships are most likely to land in the $3.5M raise and the ones after it. For the $2M due in four months, your existing investors and EMD partners stay the backstop.

gap.narrative: Pinemount’s model works: every project is capitalized through to construction financing, and your investors have stepped up for every equity top-up so far. What’s changed on these two is the check size, not the track record. Top-ups on $100M+ projects are bigger than friends and family have been asked for before, an EMD makes little sense when most of a raise is done, and the headlines are making new real estate investors hesitant even as rental fundamentals hold up.
gap.principle: Raising deal by deal is a bench problem. The variable you control is how many qualified, new investor relationships you add before each top-up is due, so no single raise depends on the same circle of people.
rows: Two construction-finance top-ups at once: roughly $3.5M in 6–8 months and $2M in about four, larger checks than your current network usually covers.
CMHC-backed construction financing needs the equity in place. Bringing in an EMD this late means carving out a raise that is already mostly done.
A new IR rep with a mandate to source investors but no pipeline of new names yet, and a LinkedIn page built for awareness, not for raising.
Two to three raises a year across six active projects keep leaning on the same investors, and every future top-up carries the same uncertainty.

segments.name: Ontario Accredited & HNW RE Investors
segments.why: Individuals with a history in private real estate LPs or syndications, who already understand CMHC-backed purpose-built rental and a sponsor’s equity top-up.

segments.name: Business Owners & Professionals
segments.why: Owners, physicians and exited founders in the GTA and Ontario showing tax-exposure signals, looking for long-hold, income-producing real estate.

segments.name: Canadian Single & Multi-Family Offices
segments.why: Larger checks per conversation. The segment we lean into if early meetings skew too small for the $3.5M top-up.

segments.name: Real Estate Event Attendees & Speakers
segments.why: Attendees at Toronto, Montreal and New York real estate and private-capital events, pre-targeted so your IR rep meets them in person.

icp.note: These segments are our starting point. A more comprehensive outline of investor targets, including minimum check sizes, geographies and exclusions, will be planned with Moshin and your IR rep during onboarding.

architecture.title: Two Raises, One Engine
architecture.subtitle: HOW TWO PROFILES FEED ONE CLOSING TEAM

cards.label: MOSHIN  ·  THE SPONSOR
cards.text: Moshin’s profile opens conversations with the most senior targets: family offices, business owners and experienced real estate LPs who want to hear from the people behind the projects. Its own audience, its own scripts, its own scorecard.

cards.label: IR REP  ·  THE CLOSER
cards.text: Your IR rep’s profile carries outreach to accredited and high-net-worth individuals, and every meeting either profile books goes to the person whose mandate is to onboard them. We source and qualify; he closes.

cards.label: THE REEF + EVENTS
cards.text: Both raises are retargeted to our 10k+ opt-in investor network and featured in Startup Deal Desk (84k+ subscribers). When your IR rep attends a Toronto, Montreal or New York event, we pre-target attendees and book meetings there.

band.label: WHY ONE RETAINER COVERS BOTH
band.text: The engine is shared: one dedicated account manager, one CRM, one weekly report split by project. And it compounds: every investor who meets you on these two raises is a warm name for the next top-up, so the bench grows with each project instead of starting over. The profile split above is our starting assumption; we’ll confirm it with Moshin and your IR rep in the first onboarding session.

cards.label: OUTREACH VOLUME
cards.text: 800 InMails and 800 connection invites per profile every month, from Moshin’s and your IR rep’s accounts, once fully warmed up. Every touch scored and hand-reviewed before it goes out.

cards.label: QUALIFIED MEETINGS
cards.unit: per week at steady state (month 2 onward)
cards.text: Conservatively 1–2 per profile per week once calibrated; strong audiences run more. Not a guarantee, but the range we plan around.

cards.label: TIME TO FIRST MEETINGS
cards.unit: weeks from kickoff to first booked calls
cards.text: Weeks one and two are setup: ICP, audiences, scripts, profile warm-up. A first meeting can land early; the full flow of meetings starts around day 30.

band.label: WHAT “QUALIFIED” MEANS, AND THE HONEST TIMELINE
band.text: A qualified meeting is an accredited or high-net-worth individual, fund or family office with a verified history of similar investments, who passed scoring and human review, completed the self-qualification form on booking, and whose briefing you approved. Raises historically take 6–12 months from first outreach to capital in the bank. We’ll have new investors on your calendar quickly; the close depends on your process and their diligence, and we’d rather you hear that from us now.

columns.label: MONTH 2  ·  NOVEMBER
columns.title: Steady Flow
bullets: Steady weekly flow to your IR rep

columns.label: MONTH 3  ·  DECEMBER
columns.title: Prove-Out & Scale
bullets: Plan for the next project top-ups

band.label: THE DECEMBER CHECKPOINT
band.text: By December you’ll have three months of real numbers on audience quality, meeting quality and conversions, as site plan approval (SPA) wraps up on the first site and ahead of the $2M top-up. That is your three-month opt-out checkpoint: continue into the $3.5M raise and the projects behind it, scale, or stop. The decision gets made on data, not on faith.

bullets: Two LinkedIn profiles (Moshin + IR rep), fully managed
Full campaign execution for both raises, end to end
The Reef retargeting & Startup Deal Desk feature
Event pre-targeting for your IR rep’s conferences
CRM, weekly reporting, A/B testing & optimization

buys.label: WHAT THAT BUYS
bullets: Both raises on one retainer, and the same engine ready for the next top-up across your six active projects
A flat fee: no commission, no success fee, no carve-out, so the equity you’ve already raised stays where it is
A qualified new-investor pipeline for your IR rep to close, instead of a mandate that starts with an empty list
In-person meetings at Toronto, Montreal or New York events, pre-booked from the people attending
The three-month opt-out means the December decision is made on real numbers, not on faith

cards.label: 1  ·  REVIEW
cards.text: Take this to ownership and your IR rep. We have Wednesday, September 30 at 11am booked for questions; Freizle, our COO, who designs the campaign strategy, can join so the people approving it hear the targeting plan first-hand.

cards.label: 2  ·  SIGN & KICK OFF
cards.text: The services agreement comes with this proposal so legal can review the terms in parallel. Once you say yes, onboarding starts that week: interviews with Moshin and your IR rep, and both LinkedIn profiles connected to our system.

cards.label: 3  ·  FIRST MEETINGS
cards.text: Both profiles are live within two weeks of kickoff. The first qualified investor conversations land in weeks three and four, then build to a steady weekly rhythm through November and into your December checkpoint, ahead of the first top-up.

band.label: WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU
band.text: Connect Moshin’s and your IR rep’s LinkedIn accounts to our system (no passwords or login credentials required). Share project summaries and your current investor list so we exclude them, plus anyone who has already passed. One 60-minute onboarding interview. A Calendly link for each of you, the events your IR rep plans to attend, and a do-not-contact list. That’s it. We handle the rest.

deliverables.text: 800 InMails and 800 connection invites per profile every month, from Moshin’s and your IR rep’s accounts, in your voice, once fully warmed up. Every InMail credit in your Sales Navigator plans gets used.
